paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Abraham got scared and said Sarah was his sister, and the whole mess landed on a king who hadn't done anything wrong. But look who steps in. God tells Abimelech, "I have kept you from sinning against Me. That is why I did not let you touch Sarah." (Genesis 20:6) Abraham's plan wasn't what protected her. God was.

Now here's the part that gets me. Abraham said, "Surely there is no fear of God in this place." (Genesis 20:11) He guessed it, and he guessed it wrong. Abimelech got up early, took God's warning seriously, and made it right. I've done the same thing with a batch I was sure would burn. I never even opened the oven door to check, and it came out fine. We can be sure of a thing and be dead wrong, and fear makes us GREAT at being sure.

And then God uses the very man who messed up. God calls Abraham a prophet who will pray for Abimelech (Genesis 20:7), and Abraham prays, and God heals (Genesis 20:17). Abraham didn't earn that spot, and God still trusted him with it. So when you stumble, baker, God doesn't toss you aside. He keeps you in His plans, and He can still use your prayers for other people. Abraham's story isn't done, and neither is yours.
